nodes.name: Hydrothermal synthesis of Ni-Mo-O precursor
nodes.procedure: The Ni-Mo-O-precursor nanorod arrays were grown on commercial nickel foam (NF) by a simple hydrothermal method. Prior to the growth of nanorods, NF was cleaned by acetone, ethanol and hydrochloric acid solution. Ni(NO3)2·6H2O (2 mmol) and Na2MoO4·2H2O (2 mmol) were dissolved in 35 mL of H2O, and then transferred into a 50 mL Teflon-lined stainless steel autoclave. A piece of cleaned NF (2×3 cm²) was immersed into the solution and placed against the wall of autoclave. Subsequently, the autoclave was maintained at 150°C for 6 h. The NF was taken out and cleaned by sonication several times to obtain Ni-MoO/NF precursor.
nodes.source_text: 2.1. Synthesis of Ni-Mo-O/NF ... The NF was taken out and cleaned by sonication several times to obtain Ni-MoO/NF precursor.

nodes.name: Two-step phosphoselenization of Ni-Mo-O/NF
nodes.procedure: To prepare the multiple-interfaces, the obtained Ni-Mo-O/NF precursor was first treated at 400°C for 2 h with a heating rate of 3°C/min under H2/Ar atmosphere to form Ni-MoOx/NF. Then, the obtained Ni-MoOx/NF sample (500 mg), NaH2PO2 (500 mg), and Se powder (50 mg) were put at three separate positions in one closed porcelain boat with Se powder and NaH2PO2 situated in the upstream. The reaction was conducted at 350°C for 2 h, with a heating rate of 5°C/min⁻¹ under 100 sccm Ar gas flow.

nodes.characterization_summary: SEM images of Ni₂P-NiSe₂/MoOₓ/NF show nanorod arrays with abundant nanoparticles on surfaces.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The typical SEM image (Fig. 2b-d) and TEM image (Fig. 2e) of Ni₂P-NiSe₂/MoOₓ/NF exhibit the nanorod arrays with an abundance of minute nanoparticles distributed across their surfaces.

nodes.characterization_summary: TEM of Ni-Mo-O/NF shows nanorods 50-100 nm diameter; Ni-MoOₓ/NF shows crystalline Ni nanoparticles on amorphous nanorods; Ni₂P-NiSe₂/MoOₓ/NF shows nanoparticles anchored on nanorods.
nodes.evidence_snippet: yielding one-dimensional nanorods with diameters in the range of 50 to 100 nm, as verified through SEM and TEM images (Fig. S3).

nodes.characterization_summary: Ni-Mo-O/NF shows NiMoO₄·xH₂O phase (JCPDS No.13-0128); Ni-MoOₓ/NF shows single Ni phase (JCPDS No.04-0850); Ni₂P-NiSe₂/MoOₓ/NF shows Ni₂P peaks at 40.8°, 44.6°, 47.3°, 54.2° (111),(201),(210),(300) and NiSe₂ peaks at 33.6°, 36.9°, 50.7°, 55.5°, 57.8° (210),(211),(311),(023),(321); no Mo peaks indicating amorphous MoOₓ.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Xray powder diffraction (XRD) pattern (Fig. S4) of Ni-Mo-O/NF confirms the crystalline nature of the NiMoO₄·xH₂O phase (JCPDS No.13-0128).

nodes.characterization_summary: STEM-EDX mapping confirms uniform Mo, O distribution along Ni-MoOₓ/NF nanorods with Ni localized in nanoparticles; Ni₂P-NiSe₂/MoOₓ/NF shows uniform Mo, O, Ni, P, Se distribution.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Detailed STEM and EDX elemental mapping (Fig. S5d-g) further confirm the uniform spatial distribution of Mo and O along the entire length of individual nanorods, with Ni exclusively localized within the nanoparticle regions.

nodes.characterization_summary: Ni-MoOₓ/NF confirms Ni⁰ and Mo⁴⁺; Ni₂P-NiSe₂/MoOₓ/NF shows Ni 2p at 852.5/869.7 eV (Niδ+), P 2p at 129.7/130.6 eV (+0.2 eV shift), Se 2p at 54.1/55.1 eV (-0.3 eV shift), Mo 3d at 228.7/232.4 eV (Mo⁴⁺); electron transfer from P→Se and MoOₓ→Ni₂P-NiSe₂.
nodes.evidence_snippet: In the high-resolution Ni 2p spectrum (Fig. 3b) of Ni₂P-NiSe₂/MoOₓ/NF, distinct peaks at 852.5 and 869.7 eV are attributed to Niδ+ (0<δ<2), corresponding to Ni-P/Se bonding.

nodes.characterization_summary: HRTEM confirms numerous interfaces between (210) planes of Ni₂P and NiSe₂ anchored on amorphous MoOₓ nanorods, consistent with SAED pattern.
nodes.evidence_snippet: High-resolution TEM images (Fig. 2f,g) affirm the generation of numerous interfaces between the (210) planes of Ni₂P and NiSe₂, firmly anchored onto the amorphous nanorods.

nodes.characterization_summary: EDX mapping shows uniform dispersion of Mo, O, Ni, P, Se across Ni₂P-NiSe₂/MoOₓ/NF nanorods.
nodes.evidence_snippet: elemental distribution analysis through energy dispersive X-ray spectroscopy (EDX) mapping images (Fig. 2h) reveal the uniform dispersion of Mo, O, Ni, P, and Se elements across the entire length of the nanorods.

nodes.characterization_summary: Ni₂P-NiSe₂/MoOₓ/NF shows Se-Se stretching at 232.7 cm⁻¹, NiP₂ peaks at 320.1, 488.4 cm⁻¹, Mo-O modes at 822.1, 898.4, 946.8 cm⁻¹; negative shift in Ni-P/Ni-Se bonds indicates electron interaction with MoOₓ.
nodes.evidence_snippet: a prominent peak at 232.7 cm⁻¹ can be unequivocally attributed to the Se-Se stretching mode of cubic NiSe₂, while two peaks at 320.1 and 488.4 cm⁻¹ are typically associated with NiP₂.

nodes.characterization_summary: All prepared samples exhibit larger specific surface area indicating porous structure.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The N₂ adsorption-desorption analysis (Fig. S10) exhibits the larger specific surface area of the prepared samples, indicating the porous structure.

nodes.characterization_summary: SAED pattern of Ni₂P-NiSe₂/MoOₓ/NF consistent with interfaces between Ni₂P and NiSe₂.
nodes.evidence_snippet: which are consistent with their selected-area electron diffraction (SAED) pattern (Fig. 2e).

nodes.characterization_summary: High-resolution XPS survey confirms presence of Mo, O, Ni, P, Se elements in Ni₂P-NiSe₂/MoOₓ/NF powder samples.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The XPS survey spectra in Fig. S11a display the presence of targeted elements including Mo, O, Ni, P, and Se in Ni₂P-NiSe₂/MoOₓ/NF.
